section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between attachment (deveikus) and connection (kesher), using the analogy of a belt versus a soul, and applies it to the distinction between sacrifices and incense.
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing the known [concept]
that connection is also higher than attachment.
For attachment is in externality,
like when a belt clings to a man's loins,
that the attachment of the belt to
(the loins of)
the man is only to his externality,
whereas connection is in internality,
like "and his soul is bound to his soul"
which reaches into his innerness.
And this is the difference between sacrifices and incense,
that the service of sacrifices is from the aspect that Israel are attached to the Holy One, blessed be He,
[as it is brought in the Midrash
and in the Zohar],
and therefore they would offer the sacrifices upon the external altar,
which in the soul of man corresponds to the externality of the heart.
And incense is a term for connection
[for every "knot" in Scripture is translated as "ketar"],
and therefore the incense is upon the inner altar,
which in the soul of man corresponds to the innerness of the heart.
And the difference between the service of the externality of the heart and the service of the innerness of the heart is,
that the service of the externality of the heart is through reason and intellect,
for in love that is through reason and intellect, change applies,
whereas the service of the innerness of the heart is above reason and intellect,
in which no change applies.
And this is that "sacrifices" is a term for drawing near,
and "incense" a term for connection,
for "drawing near" indicates that it is a [separate] entity,
except that it is close to Divinity,
but it is possible that it may distance itself, Heaven forbid,
whereas connection
(incense)
is a permanent bond,
for the true meaning of a permanent bond is that no change applies to it.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between attachment and connection in the service from below to above (sacrifices and incense) and in the drawing down from above to below (Torah and charity).
section.t: And behold, this distinction between attachment and connection is in the service from below to above.
For sacrifices and incense are both the pillar of service,
which is an elevation from below to above.
And the distinction between attachment and connection regarding the drawing down from above to below
(Torah and acts of kindness)
is as it is brought in the Zohar:
"How beloved are Israel before the Holy One, blessed be He... and He desires to attach Himself to them and to connect with them."
And the Mitteler Rebbe explains
that "to attach Himself to them" is through the mitzvos,
for the drawing down through the mitzvos is in the aspect of encompassing [light],
as it is written,
"and His right hand embraces me,"
that the light drawn down through the mitzvos embraces the person who performs the mitzvos,
for an embrace is from the outside,
and therefore it says "to attach Himself to them,"
for attachment is an external connection.
And "to connect with them" is through the Torah,
for the drawing down through the Torah is in internality, as it is written,
"and Your Torah is within my innards."
And therefore it says "and to connect with them,"
for connection is an internal connection.
For the connection of the Holy One, blessed be He, with Israel through the Torah is called "connection,"
as per the statement,
"Three knots
are connected one with another:
the Holy One, blessed be He,
the Torah, and Israel."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains two aspects of Israel's attachment to God—one regarding vessels (external unity) and one regarding lights (essential unity)—and why even the attachment of lights is called "attachment."
section.t: And behold, regarding the attachment of Israel to the Holy One, blessed be He,
[from which aspect they have the power to offer sacrifices]
there are two matters.
For in the Midrash
it is brought that this that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded Israel to offer sacrifices is because they are attached to Me, as it is written,
"for as a belt clings to a man's loins," etc.
And in the Zohar
it is brought: "Fortunate are Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, called them 'Adam'... 'Adam, when one of you brings an offering,'
why did He call them 'Adam'? Because it is written,
'And you who cling to the Lord your God.'"
And it is explained in the continuation of 5666,
that the Midrash speaks about the matter of the attachment of vessels,
that the vessels are
in the aspect of [separate] existence, and their unity
(the attachment)
is not an essential unity,
and therefore it brings the verse "as a belt clings," etc., that the belt is an entity unto itself except that it is attached to the man,
whereas the Zohar speaks about the matter of the attachment of lights,
that the attachment and unity of lights is an essential unity,
and therefore it brings the verse "and you who cling to the Lord your God,"
a literal attachment.
And it may be said,
that this that even the attachment of lights is called by the name "attachment,"
for attachment is in externality
(as above),
is because even the light is an extension and revelation that is outside the essence.
